questions.stem: Explain why implicit coercion can lead to bugs in a program. Provide an example to illustrate your explanation.
markingGuide: Implicit coercion can cause unexpected behavior if the programmer is not aware of the conversions.
Example of a language where `"5" + 3` results in "53" instead of 8.

questions.explanation: Implicit coercion automatically converts types, which can lead to unexpected results if the programmer assumes a different type. For instance, adding a string and a number might concatenate them instead of performing arithmetic, leading to logical errors.

questions.stem: Discuss the trade-offs between static and dynamic type checking. Include at least two advantages and disadvantages of each.
markingGuide: Static: Early error detection, optimized performance.
Static: Less flexibility, more verbose code.
Dynamic: Greater flexibility, easier to write code.
Dynamic: Runtime errors, potential performance overhead.
